summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, and chronic systolic heart failure, was admitted for severe shortness of breath and atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. He presented with fluid overload, confirmed by chest imaging showing pulmonary edema and cardiomegaly. Initial management included BiPAP, intravenous diltiazem for rate control, and emergent hemodialysis to reduce volume. During the hospitalization, he was diagnosed with amiodarone-induced hyperthyroidism, which was contributing to his arrhythmia, and was started on methimazole. On day three, he developed new-onset right foot drop with sensory loss; imaging ruled out stroke, DVT, or spinal compression, and the finding was attributed to sciatic nerve compression, likely from prolonged positioning or a blood pressure cuff. He showed improvement in respiratory status and was transitioned to oral medications. Due to persistent mobility issues, he was discharged to an extended care rehabilitation facility with plans for physical therapy, medication management, and follow-up with endocrinology and nephrology.
